nodes.summary: Let $\Gamma$ be a $k$-regular Cayley graph on a group $G$ with generating set $S$. For $n \ge 1$, the first-return probability of $\Gamma$ at time $n$ is the real number obtained by dividing by $k^n$ the number of words $(s_1, \dots, s_n) \in S^n$ with $s_1 s_2 \cdots s_n = 1$ and $s_1 \cdots s_m \ne 1$ for every $0 < m < n$; at time $n = 0$ it is $0$.
nodes.title: First-return probability

nodes.summary: For a group $G$ and a natural number $k$, the data of a $k$-regular Cayley graph on $G$ is a finite set $S \subseteq G$ of generators such that $S$ is closed under inverses ($s \in S$ implies $s^{-1} \in S$), the identity $1$ does not belong to $S$, every element of $G$ is the product of a finite (possibly empty) list of elements of $S$, and $S$ has exactly $k$ elements.
nodes.title: Regular Cayley graph

nodes.summary: For every natural number $k > 1$ there is a real number $C < 1$ such that for every group $G$ and every $k$-regular Cayley graph $\Gamma$ on $G$ whose return probability is less than $1$, the return probability of $\Gamma$ is at most $C$.
nodes.title: Uniform return-probability gap for transient Cayley graphs

nodes.summary: The statement that for every natural number $k > 1$ there is a real number $C < 1$ such that for every group $G$ and every $k$-regular Cayley graph $\Gamma$ on $G$, if the return probability of $\Gamma$ is less than $1$ (that is, $\Gamma$ is transient), then it is at most $C$.
nodes.title: Uniform return-probability gap

nodes.summary: The return probability of a $k$-regular Cayley graph $\Gamma$ is the sum $\sum_{n \ge 0} p_n$, where $p_n$ is the first-return probability of $\Gamma$ at time $n$.
nodes.title: Return probability
